subject.title: [Bug]: Gateway heap grows to 1073MB+ at idle on macOS, cron jobs fail silently under memory pressure (ref #86613, #86509)

question: Should #87109 be resolved by proving current main no longer reproduces, or should OpenClaw add durable restart-aware cron failure reporting that does not depend on the wedged Gateway event loop?
rationale: The codebase has partial fixes for the likely memory and event-loop causes, but deciding whether in-process cron alerts are sufficient under Gateway pressure is a product/architecture choice rather than a narrow autonomous repair.

options.title: Validate current main first
options.body: Run the macOS launchd soak with the reporter's memory_search and cron shape, then close only if heap/RSS, restart behavior, and failureAlert delivery are proven fixed.

options.title: Add durable cron lifecycle reporting
options.body: If the soak still fails, add started/no-success recovery or externalized failure reporting so cron failures surface after timeout or restart even when the Gateway event loop is unhealthy.

options.title: Close as covered by related fixes
options.body: Treat #86701, #86783, and #100867 as sufficient and close now, accepting the risk that the combined macOS cron scenario was never revalidated.

recommendation.title: Validate current main first
recommendation.body: Run the macOS launchd soak with the reporter's memory_search and cron shape, then close only if heap/RSS, restart behavior, and failureAlert delivery are proven fixed.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc is the strongest current routing candidate across the macOS Gateway correction and adjacent QMD/memory history, while the remaining choice spans multiple owners.
